Member ID: W298663271
Reference number: POC-E84DB56372-39024
Date of denial notice: 2026-08-17
Requested service/CPT: 63030 (Lower back disc surgery / decompression)
Treating surgeon: Duval, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To the HealthPartners Appeals Committee:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 63030, communicated in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-17 (reference POC-E84DB56372-39024). The stated reason for denial was that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." I respectfully disagree and ask that this decision be reversed based on the clinical record summarized below, which I believe satisfies the coverage criteria in HealthPartners' "Spinal decompression surgeries" policy (https://www.healthpartners.com/ucm/groups/public/@hp/@public/@cc/documents/documents/entry_256055.pdf).

[Note to reviewer: I have not been able to confirm the exact policy number or effective/revision date printed on this document, as none was visible in the copy I was able to obtain. I am relying on the coverage-criteria language that HealthPartners has publicly posted under this title, and I ask that HealthPartners confirm which specific version of its criteria (including any MCG, InterQual, or other third-party criteria) was applied to my prior authorization request, and provide me a copy of it.]

That policy states that decompression surgery is covered "when all of the following criteria are met," and I address each one below using the documentation already in my prior authorization packet.

1. Diagnosis of a condition causing spinal cord and/or nerve root compression
The policy requires "Clinical documentation indicates presence/diagnosis of a condition or conditions causing spinal cord and/or nerve root compression," including as an example "Herniated disc." My MRI of the lumbar spine, performed 2026-06-25, documents an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root. This is precisely the type of finding contemplated by this criterion.

2. Qualifying sign/symptom limiting activities of daily living
The policy requires "at least one sign/symptom, associated with the condition(s), limiting activities of daily living," and lists "Radiculopathy" and "Upper/lower extremity weakness, numbness, or pain" as examples. I have had 14 months of progressive lower back pain unrelieved by rest, with radicular pain radiating into my right calf, and I am unable to stand for more than 10 minutes at a time. On examination, I have a positive provocative test on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level (L4-L5/L5 nerve root). This satisfies the symptom and functional-limitation criterion.

3. Radiographic confirmation supporting the indication for surgery
The policy requires "radiographic results (e.g., plain radiographs, advanced imaging studies), confirming the presence of spinal cord and/or nerve root compression caused by the condition(s) and supporting the indication for the decompression surgery." The 2026-06-25 lumbar MRI directly confirms compression of the traversing L5 nerve root at L4-L5 due to disc extrusion and severe lateral recess stenosis, correlating with my clinical exam findings (positive provocative testing and a neurologic deficit at the same level). This is the imaging evidence the denial states was lacking, and I ask that the reviewer re-examine the MRI report and images in light of this criterion.

4. Failure of at least 8 weeks of intensive conservative treatment, including physical therapy
The policy requires that symptoms "persist despite completion of at least 8 weeks of intensive conservative treatments (such as exercise, medication use, or chiropractic care)," with physical therapy of "at least 4 visits over a course of 6 weeks or less" within the current episode of care, and notes physical therapist's notes must be submitted. I have exceeded this requirement:
- I completed a supervised course of physical therapy, including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility work, over 12 weeks (2026-03-28 to 2026-06-20), totaling 20 visits, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- I used NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief.
- I received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-30, which provided only 2 weeks of partial relief.
Despite this extensive conservative treatment, my symptoms have persisted and progressed over 14 months, satisfying this criterion.

Additional relevant information
I have no active infection and no untreated substance use disorder, my BMI is 29, and I am a non-smoker — factors that support my candidacy for surgery and do not implicate any of the "Indications that are not covered" listed in the policy (which address laser, percutaneous/endoscopic, and annulus-repair-device procedures, none of which apply to my requested open decompression, CPT 63030).

Taken together, the MRI findings, physical examination, and 14-month history of progressive, functionally limiting radicular pain that has failed medication, injection, and a substantial, well-documented course of physical therapy meet each of the four numbered criteria in the policy quoted above. I therefore ask that HealthPartners reverse the denial and authorize CPT 63030 as requested by my surgeon, Dr. Duval.

Enclosed/attached with this appeal:
- MRI lumbar spine report, 2026-06-25
- Physical therapy discharge note (12-week course, 2026-03-28 to 2026-06-20, 20 visits)
- Medication history documenting 8 months of NSAID use
- Record of corticosteroid injection, 2026-04-30, and response
- Office notes documenting provocative testing and neurologic exam findings
- Letter of medical necessity from Dr. Duval, Orthopedic Surgery
- [Any additional records not listed above]

Please treat this as a formal appeal under HealthPartners' complaints and appeals process. I understand I have 180 days from the date of the denial notice (2026-08-17), or until 2027-02-13, to submit this appeal, and I am submitting well within that window. Given the severity of my functional limitation (inability to stand more than 10 minutes, progressive radicular symptoms), I also request that this appeal be handled as expeditiously as possible; please advise if I should separately request an expedited review.

I can be reached at [phone number] or [email address] with any questions or requests for additional information. Please send your written determination to the address/email above.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Skyler Jennings
